determination.basis: Work of the United States Government, not subject to copyright in the US (17 U.S.C. §105). NASA's media guidelines: 'NASA content … generally are not subject to copyright in the United States. You may use this material for educational or informational purposes … This general permission extends to personal Web pages.' The quoted page addresses images, audio, video and media files explicitly; the status of NASA-authored text rests on §105 rather than on that sentence. Full text ships in the feed (~6,096 chars median measured).
conditions: The NASA insignia and logotype are protected and are not covered by this.
Third-party and contractor-authored material NASA republishes (e.g. JPL/Caltech) is not a US Government work and may be copyrighted; NASA-authored text is the target here.

AI outputs: the same page states 'attribution of the information directly to NASA is not permitted' for content incorporated into a language model, and 'All outputs from the AI model should be attributed to the AI product itself, not NASA. References like "according to NASA" or similar are prohibited in AI products.' A generated summary must not be presented as NASA's words; the source row may say the material came from NASA.

17 U.S.C. §105 places US Government works in the public domain IN THE UNITED STATES; this deployment is not in the US (Legal A-L3), and the wider reuse rests on NASA's stated permission for informational use rather than on §105 alone.

Body use is excluded separately: 'you shall not modify, copy, translate, create a derivative work of … any content' and 'You may not use … any content … to build or train large language models, machine learning tools, or artificial intelligence (AI) systems.' A generated summary is a derivative work, so the feed is permitted and the body is not.
conditions: Display 'NPR' or 'NPR News Headlines' adjacent to the feed content.

determination.basis: CORRECTED 15 Sep 2026 — an earlier reading recorded CC BY-SA 3.0 from a licence URL found in the feed; that was an image credit inside one article, not the publisher's licence, and the live feed carries no licence element. The terms: 'Copyright © 2026 IPS-Inter Press Service. All rights reserved.' Reprint policy: 'Republication or any other distribution of IPS materials is encouraged, but is only possible after written agreement of IPS … Users can choose to pay either a subscription fee … or to pay a republication fee per article. Different rates and conditions apply for commercial and non-profit users. In some cases, reproduction rights can be granted for free.' Body use is therefore refused without agreement. Feed display is not addressed — IPS publishes RSS feeds for readers — so this is headline_only ON SILENCE, a weaker basis than NPR's express permission. The feed ships full text; the tier is set to extraction so no body is stored.
conditions: Never store or summarize the body — all rights reserved.
A free non-profit reproduction licence is available on request ('In some cases, reproduction rights can be granted for free'); that is the route to body_text, not a re-reading.

determination.basis: CORRECTED 15 Sep 2026 — an earlier reading recorded the terms as unreadable; they are readable once the script-embedded page text is extracted. Sky.com Terms and Conditions apply to 'Sky's websites, platforms, services, products and apps including sky.com'. Clause 2.8: 'You will not access, search and/or collect data from … any Sky Service … by any means (whether automated or manual) unless Sky has given its express written authorisation to do so. This means that, among other things, (a) you may not use any robots, bots, spiders, crawlers, devices, scripts or other data gathering or extraction software and/or tools, whether automated or manual, to access, acquire, copy, monitor, scrape, data mine, or aggregate any Content or any portion of the Sky Service for any purpose, and (b) you may not use any Content for the purpose of directly or indirectly training, developing or improving a software tool or service, including any artificial intelligence tool, model, system or platform.' The same shape as AP's clause. robots.txt on news.sky.com says '# Disallow news aggregators except on RSS.', which reads as Sky contemplating aggregators on the feed — but a robots.txt comment is not the 'express written authorisation' clause 2.8 requires, and this file does not assume it is. REFUSED unless that reading is ruled otherwise.
conditions: Do not enable. Determined 15 Sep 2026: the robots.txt aggregator comment is not treated as the express written authorisation clause 2.8 requires. Reopening this needs a licence or written authorisation from Sky, not a re-reading.
